articles.body: You have company domains from a trade-show exhibitor list or a CRM export and want to know which run Shopify, WordPress or WooCommerce, Webflow, Wix or Squarespace. A Shopify app vendor sizing its market, a WordPress agency, a migration consultancy: all need the same table. This is research about companies and their public websites, not about people. articles.title: The runtime cost of string encryption in a hot loop (and how to scope it)
articles.excerpt: String encryption is one of the cheapest, highest-value transforms Nebula.NET applies: it turns every readable literal in your assembly — API endpoints, format strings, license messages, the names of…
articles.body: String encryption is one of the cheapest, highest-value transforms Nebula.NET applies: it turns every readable literal in your assembly — API endpoints, format strings, license messages, the names of things — into an encoded blob that is decoded only at runtime. Open the protected binary in a decompiler and the roadmap those literals used to draw is gone. For the overwhelming majority of code, it is free in every sense that matters. The one place it is not free is a hot loop. An encrypted literal is decrypted at the point of use , and "the point of use" can be inside a method that runs millions of times. A decode that costs a few nanoseconds is invisible once; multiplied across a tight inner loop it becomes something you can measure.

articles.title: No Docker tag has been generated by docker/metadata-action
articles.excerpt: No Docker tag has been generated is a warning from docker/metadata-action saying that none of its tag rules produced a version for the event that is running. It is a statement about the event and the…
articles.body: No Docker tag has been generated is a warning from docker/metadata-action saying that none of its tag rules produced a version for the event that is running. It is a statement about the event and the tags input together, and it is never caused by leaving images out. Each default rule tests github.ref against one regular expression. If every rule declines, version.main is never set and getTags returns an empty array. What this error means The metadata step is green. It writes two warnings, one about a version and one about a tag, and then sets tags and version to empty strings. The build step that reads them either pushes an image with no tag at all or fails a little later complaining about the tag it was handed.

articles.title: UAV Balloon Popper
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the MLH x DEV Writing Challenge Sometime after midnight at HackUMass, I held a phone up to a Raspberry Pi camera. The phone showed a picture of a red balloon. On the table, a…
articles.body: This is a submission for the MLH x DEV Writing Challenge What I Built Sometime after midnight at HackUMass, I held a phone up to a Raspberry Pi camera. The phone showed a picture of a red balloon. On the table, a 3D-printed flying wing twitched its elevons. When I moved the phone left, the wing banked left. When I moved it up, the nose pitched up. The plane couldn't see me or the phone, only the balloon, and it was trying to fly at it. That was UAV Balloon Popper , a small autonomous plane that hunts down stray balloons. Why balloons? The idea started with drones. Watching the war in Ukraine, I kept seeing the same problem: cheap drones are cheap to build and expensive to stop. Interceptor missiles can cost far more than the drones they shoot down.

articles.title: How Agentic Commerce Actually Works: A Developer Guide to ChatGPT Wallet
articles.excerpt: How Agentic Commerce Actually Works: A Developer Guide to ChatGPT Wallet ChatGPT can now buy things for you. As developers, we need to understand what is happening under the hood. Last week OpenAI lau…
articles.body: How Agentic Commerce Actually Works: A Developer Guide to ChatGPT Wallet ChatGPT can now buy things for you. As developers, we need to understand what is happening under the hood. Last week OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet in beta. Users can save a card, ask ChatGPT to buy something, approve with biometrics, and the order is placed. It sounds simple. For developers, it is a massive shift in how the web works. For 30 years, the flow was like this: User searches, user clicks, user pays. We optimized for SEO, landing pages, and checkout conversion. Now the flow is like this: User talks to AI, AI searches, AI decides, AI pays. The user may never visit your website. This is called agentic commerce. And if you build websites, APIs, or SaaS products, you need to prepare for it now.

articles.title: How escaping gases ripped apart a comet and caused it to become thousands of times brighter
articles.excerpt: This summer, comet 220P/McNaught burst into life out of nowhere to become one of the year’s highlights for amateur astronomers.
articles.body: A comet dazzled this summer as the sun’s heat caused ice beneath its surface to turn to gas and rip out through its surface, spewing hundreds of billions of pounds' worth of dust into space and causing the comet to brighten by thousands of times. Comet 220P/McNaught was discovered by the prolific Australian comet discoverer Robert McNaught in 2004. It is a periodic comet, the 220th discovered, meaning that it comes back again and again on a regular basis – in 220P’s case, once every five-and-a-half years when it gets about as close to the sun as Mars . Other than that, 220P is fairly nondescript, usually languishing at a feeble brightness fainter than magnitude +15, out of reach of most amateur telescopes. There has been little else to say about the comet, until this year.

articles.title: What's next for SpaceX's Starship after epic Flight 15 chopsticks catch?
articles.excerpt: SpaceX just made spaceflight history, catching the upper stage of its Starship megarocket when it returned to Earth. But Starship still has some pretty big boxes left to check.
articles.body: Starship may have just made history, but it still has some work to do to get fully up and running. The megarocket launched on its 15th test flight on Friday (Nov. 13), aiming to pull off a dramatic and unprecedented twofer. SpaceX wanted to bring both Starship elements — its Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage — back to the launch pad at its Starbase site in Texas to be caught by the tower's "chopstick" arms. It didn't happen with Super Heavy; the booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday evening after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship came home successfully , nestling into the tower's arms in a soft and unprecedented embrace on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), 22.5 hours after lifting off. Long-distance view of Ship's historic landing on Nov. 14, 2026.

articles.title: This Week In Space podcast: Episode 236 — Alienspotting
articles.excerpt: On Episode 236 of This Week In Space, Tariq Malik and Rod Pyle are joined by Mikhail Tikhonov to talk about how life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize.
articles.body: On Episode 236 of This Week In Space , Tariq Malik and Rod Pyle are joined by Mikhail Tikhonov to talk about how life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize. When we think of extraterrestrials, our minds generally go from the latex-suited bipedal aliens seen in Star Trek and Star Wars to more exotic critters in sci-fi movies. Scientists think in terms of carbon-based microbial life and other lower life forms. But some researchers, such as Tikhonov from Washington University, suggest that life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize. He further suggests a new definition of life: something that takes in and transforms energy and replicates. His ideas radically expand our notions of alien life and how it might be recognized.

articles.title: 'Alien: Fireteam Elite 2' is a good old-fashioned bug hunt, ironically plagued by bugs
articles.excerpt: We're scared of the Xenomorphs again, but Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 knows old-fashioned bug hunts shouldn't be a thing of the past.
articles.body: The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games , and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel. At Summer Game Fest 2026 , we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong? Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years.
articles.author: Fran Ruiz

articles.title: The OpenAI board member who fired Sam Altman says we still can’t trust AI CEOs
articles.excerpt: Today, I’m talking with Helen Toner, the executive director of the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University. This episode is part two of our series on AI in real life. Hele…
articles.body: Today, I’m talking with Helen Toner, the executive director of the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University. This episode is part two of our series on AI in real life. Helen is a well-known figure in the AI safety and policy community, though she is perhaps best known for having served on the board of OpenAI, when she was one of four board members who voted to fire Sam Altman . That incident, now sometimes referred to as “the blip,” ended with Sam coming back as CEO, Helen resigning, and a new board of directors. OpenAI has since restructured entirely .
articles.author: Nilay Patel
